University AI Policy Guide

This comprehensive policy describes responsible use of generative artificial intelligence across academic departments, research laboratories, and administrative offices. Faculty and students must follow data classification rules before entering institutional records into external large language model tools. If you encounter an "Access Denied" message while logging into the campus enterprise AI portal, contact the IT Help Desk with your campus ID to verify group membership and multi-factor authentication enrollment. Additional guidance covers citation practices, syllabus disclosure templates, accessibility standards, and procurement security reviews for new AI software vendors across all colleges and schools.

Paragraph two extends the documentation well beyond fifteen hundred characters so corroborated challenge detection distinguishes genuine documentation from short WAF interstitials. Departments offering courses in machine learning, natural language processing, and data science should publish clear guidelines in each syllabus specifying which AI assistants are permitted for brainstorming, debugging, and writing support. Research groups requesting high-performance GPU cluster allocations can submit proposals through the Office of Research Computing portal each semester. Student organizations hosting hackathons or AI literacy workshops may request cloud credits and faculty advisors through Student Affairs.

Paragraph three documents common authentication and network troubleshooting steps, including resolving VPN routing issues, clearing stale cookies, and requesting role upgrades when seeing an Access Denied notice on restricted intranet tools. Always verify that sensitive FERPA or HIPAA protected datasets remain on approved university infrastructure.
